questions: What does "replace each of A_i and A_{i+1}" mean exactly - do both A_i and A_{i+1} become 1, or is there a specific condition for which one gets replaced?
Are the indices i, i+1, i+2 in the operations considered modulo N when they exceed N, given that S_{N+1}=S_1 and A_{N+1}=A_1 are defined?
Can we perform the same operation multiple times on the same positions, or are there restrictions on how many times an operation can be applied to a specific index?
When checking if a good string exists, do we need to find at least one valid string S, or must all possible strings S be checked?
Is it guaranteed that the sequence A will have at least one 0 initially, or could it already consist entirely of 1s?
What happens if N < 3, since the operations require checking three consecutive characters but the constraint states 3 ≤ N?
Do the operations modify the original sequence A permanently, or is a copy of A used for each simulation with string S?
When performing the operations, if A_i or A_{i+1} is already 1, does "replacing" it have any effect or is it simply left unchanged?
answers: We replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with the value 1.
Yes, indices wrap around modulo N as given by S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, A_{N+1}=A_1.
Not specified beyond 'any number of times,' which permits repeating operations on the same or overlapping indices.
We need to determine whether there EXISTS at least one good string S, as stated -- not check all possible strings exhaustively.
Not guaranteed; A could already consist entirely of 1s, in which case zero operations are needed.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 3.
Not specified beyond what's given; each candidate string S is evaluated by simulating the operations on A starting from its original given state.
Replacing an already-1 value with 1 has no effect, since 'replace with 1' simply sets the value to 1 regardless of its prior state.
inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, consisting only of uppercase English letters, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero) so that the sequence A contains no 0. Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with the value 1. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
